The AI Product Management internship in short

The SkillMe AI Product Management internship is a 4-week, fully remote programme open to students worldwide. Over four weekly milestones you build SmartRecap: AI Meeting Notes Feature, post each milestone publicly on LinkedIn, and have it reviewed against clear acceptance criteria. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month, and interns who get 3 of 4 milestones approved earn a QR-verified certificate and a Letter of Recommendation.

Week by week

What each week of the AI Product Management internship covers

The four milestones of SmartRecap: AI Meeting Notes Feature.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Problem Framing and Competitive Analysis

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Pick a real AI feature idea (an AI meeting-notes summarizer for a team collaboration tool), talk to potential users about the problem, and study how existing products solve it. Good PM work starts with a sharp problem statement, not a feature list.

    What you learn

    • Framing an AI feature around a user problem, not a technology
    • Running short user interviews to validate a problem exists
    • Structuring a competitive analysis for AI features specifically
    • Writing a clear problem statement and success metric

    What you submit

    • Interview questions and notes, or survey results
    • A competitive analysis of 3 existing AI meeting-notes products
    • A one-paragraph problem statement
    • A defined success metric with a one-sentence justification
  2. Week 2 of 4

    PRD and Prompt/Eval Spec

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Turn last week's research into a full PRD for the AI meeting-notes feature, plus a lightweight prompt and eval spec — the artifact that tells engineers not just what to build, but how to judge whether the AI part is actually working. This is the core skill that separates AI PM work from general PM work.

    What you learn

    • Structuring a PRD for a feature with a probabilistic (AI-generated) component
    • Writing user stories and acceptance criteria for an AI feature
    • Designing a lightweight prompt spec: inputs, instructions, and output format
    • Defining an eval spec: what 'good enough' output looks like and how to check for it

    What you submit

    • A full PRD covering problem, goals/non-goals, user stories and functional requirements
    • 4-6 user stories with objectively checkable acceptance criteria
    • A prompt spec defining inputs, instructions and required output format
    • An eval spec with 8-10 example cases and expected content plus a named failure mode
  3. Week 3 of 4

    Clickable Spec and Stakeholder Narrative

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Turn the PRD into something people can actually react to: a clickable spec or lightweight prototype showing the feature in context, plus a stakeholder narrative explaining trade-offs. PMs ship decisions and clarity, not just documents — this week is about making the feature tangible before any engineer writes code.

    What you learn

    • Building a clickable spec or lightweight prototype without code (Figma, or a slide-based clickthrough)
    • Writing a stakeholder narrative that explains trade-offs, not just features
    • Anticipating and addressing likely engineering and design pushback in writing
    • Prioritizing scope for a first version (v1) versus later iterations

    What you submit

    • A clickable prototype or spec with at least 4-6 linked screens
    • A one-page stakeholder narrative covering rationale, scope and biggest risk
    • A list of 3 likely objections with planned mitigations
    • A v1 scope cut of the PRD's requirements with reasons for each cut
  4. Week 4 of 4

    Launch Plan, Metrics Dashboard Spec and Case Study

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Close the loop from idea to launch: write a lightweight launch plan and a metrics dashboard spec for measuring the feature post-launch, then publish a full case study telling the whole story from research to spec. This is the deliverable a hiring manager or team would actually read to judge your PM thinking end to end.

    What you learn

    • Writing a lightweight launch plan (phasing, rollout, guardrails)
    • Specifying a metrics dashboard for an AI feature (adoption, quality, safety signals)
    • Structuring a PM case study that tells a complete, honest story
    • Presenting a body of product work clearly to an outside reader

    What you submit

    • A lightweight launch plan with rollout phasing and a guardrail
    • A metrics dashboard spec with 6-8 metrics and their exact data sources
    • A stated kill-or-iterate decision rule tied to real metrics
    • A published end-to-end case study linking all four weeks of work, with a self-critical reflection

AI Product Management internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the AI Product Management internship?

You build SmartRecap: AI Meeting Notes Feature. Take an AI feature from a rough idea to a PRD, an eval spec, a competitive analysis and a clickable prototype — the full product thinking loop, no repo required. It is one project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

Is the AI Product Management internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. The stipend is performance-based and is not paid to every intern: it goes to the interns whose reviewed work stands out in their cohort.

Who reviews my work?

Every weekly submission is reviewed against that week's acceptance criteria by the SkillMe team, which includes engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Work that misses the bar comes back with notes on what to fix.

Do I need experience to apply for the AI Product Management internship?

You need the basics of PRDs, AI Evals, Roadmapping, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at Beginner level and week 4 reaches Intermediate+. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How long is the internship and how much time does it take?

It runs for 4 weeks with one milestone a week. Each milestone is planned for about 2-3 hours, and it is fully remote, so you work at your own pace around college or a job.

Who can apply? Is it open outside India?

Anyone can apply, from any country, college or year, and we encourage you to. Selection is competitive: every application is read by a person, and shortlisted applicants hear back within 48 hours.

What do I get when I finish?

An offer letter when you are selected, a public portfolio page with every approved milestone, and a QR-verified certificate and Letter of Recommendation once 3 of your 4 milestones are approved. Top performers also earn the stipend and are referred to hiring partners.
